name: ScoreApp
tagline: Builds scored quizzes and scorecards that capture leads and hand back a personalized result report.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The mechanics here are not hard: questions, weighted answers, a score, a branch into one of a few result buckets, an email gate, a lead row in a database. An agent can produce that in a sitting and it will work fine for one scorecard you own. What you are actually buying from ScoreApp is everything around the quiz: a builder your non-technical colleague can edit, native pipes into your email tool and CRM, embed snippets that behave on someone else's marketing site, and funnel analytics that tell you where people bail. The DIY version also leaves you holding email deliverability, which is the least fun part of any lead capture tool. Fine if you want one quiz for one offer, annoying if quizzes are a repeated part of how you sell.
coreLoopDIY: Defines a quiz in a config file, scores the answers, gates the personalized result page behind an email capture, and stores leads locally with CSV export.
requirements: Node 20 and somewhere to host it
SMTP or Resend credentials if you want result emails sent
A domain or subdomain if you plan to embed it on a real site
whatYouLose: A visual quiz builder, so every question change is a code or config edit
Native integrations with email platforms, CRMs and Zapier: you get a CSV and a webhook
Funnel analytics per question, drop-off reporting and A/B testing of result copy
Deliverability infrastructure for the result email, which you now own
Templates and conversion patterns copied from thousands of quizzes that already converted
moatNotes: The lock-in is downstream: once leads with scores are flowing into your CRM and automations are triggered by result buckets, swapping the quiz engine means rewiring the whole sequence.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the quiz is the cheap part and the plumbing is not. Marketers buy this so they can ship a scorecard on Tuesday without a developer, have it embed cleanly on a WordPress landing page, push tagged leads straight into ActiveCampaign or HubSpot, and then look at a chart showing that question four is killing completion. A self-hosted version gives you the quiz and the leads, but every one of those adjacent conveniences becomes a small project you maintain forever.
notes: Great fit if you need exactly one scorecard and can edit JSON; bad fit if quizzes are a weekly marketing habit.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted scored quiz and lead capture app. Stack: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, and SQLite via better-sqlite3. No auth provider, no analytics SDK, no telemetry.

In scope:
1. Quizzes are defined in /quizzes/*.json. Each file has: slug, title, intro copy, an array of questions (single choice, multi choice, or numeric scale), per-answer point weights, and an array of result buckets with a score range, a heading, body markdown, and an optional CTA link.
2. A public quiz route at /q/[slug] that renders one question per screen with a progress bar, keeps answers in local component state, and works on mobile.
3. After the last question, show an email gate: name and email, a consent checkbox with configurable copy. On submit, POST answers plus contact details to /api/submit.
4. /api/submit computes the total score server side (never trust client scoring), picks the matching result bucket, writes a row to SQLite (quiz slug, name, email, score, bucket, raw answers JSON, user agent, created_at), and returns a signed result token.
5. A result page at /r/[token] rendering the bucket heading, body, the score, and the CTA. Tokens are HMAC signed with a secret from .env so results are not enumerable.
6. Optional result email: if RESEND_API_KEY is set in .env, send the result page link to the submitted address. If it is not set, skip silently and log locally. Do not block submission on email failure.
7. An admin page at /admin behind a single password from .env (simple cookie session, no user table) listing submissions with score, bucket and date, filterable by quiz, plus a Download CSV button.
8. An embed route /embed/[slug] with no site chrome, plus a copyable iframe snippet shown on /admin.
9. Seed the repo with one working example quiz of 6 questions and 3 result buckets so it runs immediately.

Out of scope: no visual quiz builder, no CRM integrations, no A/B testing, no multi-tenant accounts, no payment handling.

Deliver a README with setup, .env.example listing SESSION_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD and optional RESEND_API_KEY, npm scripts for dev and build, and a note on where the SQLite file lives and how to back it up.
